pairLinking.boundary: Finite target minimum below one, link mode two, pair option one, original admitted descriptor map and valid local scratch. Numeric-map parity selects adjacent logical positions without proving partner presence. Zero logical index with an odd nonexcluded map word zero-extends the decremented index into a far positive address. Descriptor admission alone is insufficient to establish pair safety. No host mask selection, live reachability or fault claim.

storage.requests: at most one request per active band when logical channels are nonzero
storage.reuse: nonnull first pointer retains the band storage
storage.partialFailure: failure stops later bands without rolling back prior writes
storage.boundary: Complete common band application storage tail with admitted active count, logical channels, stable disjoint state and completing allocator ABI. Enabled byte one permits at most one first-channel shared telemetry request per active band. Existing first pointers suppress requests; returns are stored before null checks. Failure stops later bands and retains earlier control/allocation writes. Other per-channel pointers remain unchanged. Legacy tail entry is joined by the separate legacy application proof. No actual capacity, allocation cleanup, external helper effects, lifetime or runtime selection claim.

storage.delayClear: only newly allocated successful delay storage
storage.reuse: nonnull pointers retained without capacity checks
storage.partialFailure: earlier control and pointer writes retained
storage.boundary: Valid old/current mode zero/one/two application with completing helpers, stable disjoint state and allocator ABI. Both revisions reach the same storage tail after coefficient writes. A missing delay pointer requests uint32(stride<<9), stores the return before checking, and clears only a successful new allocation. Optional storage is requested only for byte one and nonzero logical count, at most once; existing storage is retained. Allocation errors retain earlier writes. Initialization resets the listed history arrays only after nonnegative application, then sets flags three. Actual capacity, allocator ownership, helper side effects, retry recovery and runtime selection remain unresolved.

meaningBoundary: Original section-one and all section-three processing modes after recorded leaf SIMD initializers execute and remain unchanged. Current section-one/three conversion and state application join serialized controls. Crossover types one/two have directly proved coefficient arithmetic and history retention; packed trigonometric and scalar helpers retain unresolved numerical boundaries. Other generator types and legacy/default profiles are byte witnesses only. Admitted finite ordinary state, readable structs, valid rounded-channel storage and scratch/telemetry buffers. Copy treated as a primitive. Complete helper equivalence, allocation admission/lifetime, CRT initializer invocation, live constant lifetime, public names and runtime activation are not established. Pair minimum selection, map handoff and unsigned adjacent-index arithmetic are directly joined to the owning descriptor proof. Some admitted sparse maps violate partner presence or local scratch bounds; these are conditional local paths, not observed runtime faults. Every valid old/current section-three mode reaches the same delay/optional storage tail. Newly allocated delay storage is cleared; existing pointers are retained without capacity checks. Allocation failure retains earlier controls and pointers. Initial history resets follow nonnegative default application. Requests, stores and local error paths are proved, not allocator capacity, ownership or retry recovery. Common band telemetry storage visits active bands in order and retains existing first-channel pointers. Each enabled missing first pointer requests a fixed buffer at most once; failures store null, stop later bands and retain earlier writes. Actual capacity and recovery remain unresolved.
